text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The parliament will start on Wednesday a four-day session to discuss and adopt the 1997 public budget.
-General Labour Confederation chief Abu Rizk said: "Budget figures are just a big lie".
--The U.N. security council unanimously approved a six-month renewal, until July 31, of the U.N. peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon.
-Lebanese parliament and a U.S. Agency for International Development signed a cooperation agreement.
-The Lebanese navy rescued 75 Syrians who had been stranded without food for three days on a small island off northern Lebanon.
-President Hrawi asked the government to justify any tax rise decision.
-Lebanon's Banque Audi reported that its profits rose 52.5 percent in 1996 to 30.71 billion Lebanese pounds ($19.8 million) from 20.14 billion pounds in 1995.
-Prime Minister Hariri said the file of former army commander General Aoun, living in exile in Paris since 1991, should be closed. A court should either convict him or find him innocent, Hariri said.
